title: Мастер-класс от Родиона Сергеевича  (A Masterclass from Rodion Sergeyevich)

segments.t: In the apartment kitchen, Rodion Sergeyevich watches Max boiling vegetables and demonstrates how plunging them into ice water immediately after draining preserves true Italian al dente texture. Impressed by the homeless man's culinary expertise, Max and Kostya sit down at the table with him for a friendly drink.
Опять вы передерживаете овощи, Максим Леонидович.
Это уж будет не аль денте.
Можно я?
После того, как вы слили воду.
Надо опустить овощи в воду со льдом.
Это и называется аль денте.
Что в переводе с итальянского означает...
Чувствуете? Неплохо?
Никогда бы не подумал.
Вы знаете.
Без обид, Артем Сергеевич.
Какие обиды?
Я там у вас в холодильнике видел.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Опять вы передерживаете овощи, Максим Леонидович.

'You are overcooking the vegetables again, Maxim Leonidovich.' Mentioning that Vika is overcooking the vegetables again Maxim moves the talk in a new direction. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Это уж будет не аль денте.
'That will not be al dente anymore.' Vika reminds Max that that will not be al dente anymore before the moment passes.
Можно я?
'May I show you?' Asking whether may he shows Vika puts Vika right on the defensive. There is no "you" needed in the Russian here: one short word states the rule for everyone in the room.
После того, как вы слили воду.

'Right after you drain the boiling water.' Around the work and kitchen, Vika sets a calm, everyday tone with Max. Even in the middle of the drama, she keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Надо опустить овощи в воду со льдом.
'You have to plunge the vegetables into ice water.' Max mentions that Vika has to plunge the vegetables into ice water so Vika sees what is at stake.
Это и называется аль денте.

'That is what is called al dente.' Claiming that that is what is called al dente sounds confident, even if Max has doubts. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
Что в переводе с итальянского означает...
'Which translated from Italian means...' Pointing out that which translated from Italian means gives Vika a sobering reality check.
Чувствуете? Неплохо?
'Do you taste the difference? Not bad, right?' Here checking whether Max tastes the difference shows Vika looking for the real truth.
Никогда бы не подумал.

'I never would have thought of that.' Realizing that he never would have thought changes how Max handles the situation. Russian stacks "never" or "nothing" together with "not", doubling the refusal for extra weight.
Вы знаете.
'You know what.' With the point and kitchen in play, Vika keeps this short reply brisk and direct. Even in the middle of the drama, she keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Без обид, Артем Сергеевич.
'No offense, Rodion Sergeyevich.' Over the point and the table, Max answers Vika without a second thought.
Какие обиды?

'None taken at all.' Turning from the masterclass to the conversation, Vika asks Max directly. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Я там у вас в холодильнике видел.

'I spotted something in your refrigerator earlier.' With the point and conversation in play, Max keeps this short reply brisk and direct. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Опять вы передерживаете овощи, Максим Леонидович.
Это уж будет не аль денте.
Можно я?
После того, как вы слили воду.
Надо опустить овощи в воду со льдом.
Это и называется аль денте.
Что в переводе с итальянского означает...
Чувствуете? Неплохо?
Никогда бы не подумал.
Вы знаете.
Без обид, Артем Сергеевич.
Какие обиды?
Я там у вас в холодильнике видел.

That wraps up this scene as at the apartment, Rodion Sergeyevich teaches Max the proper Italian ice-bath method for cooking al dente vegetables and bonds with Max and Kostya over drinks. Until next time!
Пока!
